mainEntity.name: Where do I even start if I’m thinking about a home addition on my house?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Start by clarifying your goals, rough budget, and whether your lot and existing structure can realistically handle an addition. Then speak with a designer or design‑build contractor to sanity‑check what’s feasible.

Most headaches come from jumping straight to picking finishes before solving space, budget, and zoning constraints. A short upfront planning phase can save months of rework and thousands of dollars.

Key factors:
- What problem you’re solving (more bedrooms, open kitchen, rental unit, etc.)
- How much you can invest comfortably, including a 10–20% contingency
- Zoning limits on height, setbacks, and lot coverage
- Structural capacity of your current foundation and framing

Spend a couple of evenings collecting inspiration, making a list of must‑haves vs. nice‑to‑haves, and pulling basic property documents. Then book consultations with reputable local contractors to validate scope, budget range, and next steps. A good contractor becomes a planning partner, not just a builder.
